seo.metaTitle: Blog Title Here | EtherTrack Insights (max 60 chars)
seo.metaDescription: Compelling 1–2 sentence summary of what the reader will learn. Include focus keyword. Keep under 155 characters.
seo.focusKeyword: primary keyword you want to rank for
seo.ogTitle: Open Graph title — what shows on LinkedIn/WhatsApp (can be same as meta title)
seo.ogDescription: OG description — what shows as preview text on social. 1–2 punchy sentences.

articleInfo.h1: The H1 that displays at the top of the article
articleInfo.subtitle: 1–2 sentence subtitle that expands on the H1 and sets reader expectations.

articleInfo.category: Carbon Markets | CCTS | Carbon Accounting | ESG | Climate Policy

heroImage.alt: Descriptive alt text for the hero image
heroImage.caption: Caption shown below the hero image
heroImage.imagePrompt: Detailed AI image generation prompt for creating the hero image. Be specific about style, colors (dark background, green accents), and content.

introduction.content: 3–5 paragraphs separated by blank lines (\n\n). Hook the reader immediately. State why this matters NOW. Tell them exactly what they'll know by the end. Do NOT use bullet points here — flowing prose only.

sections.heading: Section 1 Heading — matches Table of Contents entry exactly
sections.content:
Main body text. Separate paragraphs with \n\n. Write in flowing prose. Be specific. Use real numbers, real regulation names, real examples. Avoid vague generalisations.

Second paragraph here.

Third paragraph here if needed.

sections.heading: Section With Info Box Example
sections.content:
Section body text here.

More content.

infoBox.type: definition | process | important | warning | alert | critical | cta-soft
infoBox.title: Info box title
infoBox.content: Info box body — keep concise. 2–4 sentences max. The engine renders this in a coloured callout box.

sections.heading: Section With Table Example
sections.content:
Introductory text before the table.

The table renders below this content.

table.title: Table title shown above the table
table.footnote: Optional footnote — source, methodology note, or caveat.

sections.heading: Section With Myth vs Fact Example
sections.content: Optional intro text before the myth vs fact grid.

mythVsFact.myth: The misconception — stated as someone would actually believe it.
mythVsFact.fact: The accurate correction — specific, not vague. Cite data or regulation if relevant.

sections.heading: Section With Case Study Example
sections.content: Optional intro text before the case study.

caseStudy.title: Case study headline — specific and outcome-focused
caseStudy.context: One sentence of context — what kind of company, sector, location.
caseStudy.situation: What was the challenge or starting point? 2–3 sentences.
caseStudy.action: What did they do? Be specific — what measures, what investments, what timeline? 3–4 sentences.
caseStudy.outcome: What was the measurable result? Use numbers. 2–3 sentences.
caseStudy.lesson: The single key takeaway from this case. 1–2 sentences.

sections.heading: Key Takeaways
items: First key takeaway — one complete, standalone sentence. Reader should be able to share this.
Fifth key takeaway — aim for 5–10 total.

faqs.question: Question exactly as someone would type it into Google?
faqs.answer: Direct, complete answer. 2–5 sentences. No fluff. If there is a specific regulation, number, or name that answers the question — use it.

relatedArticles.title: Related Article Title
relatedArticles.description: One sentence describing what the related article covers.

cta.headline: One compelling line that connects the article topic to what EtherTrack does.
cta.subheadline: 1–2 sentences explaining the specific value EtherTrack provides for this audience.
cta.note: No commitment · 30-minute live walkthrough · Response within 24 hours
